title: Signshot — After dinner
proposedScene: After dinner: a modest dinner still life in available light, inspired by the archived dinner photograph. A new capture, edition, and transaction recording are still required.

segments.title: The photograph
segments.voiceover: This is Signshot: a creative camera for Solana Seeker. Make a photograph you love. Then decide what happens to it.
segments.visual: Open on the real hero photograph, then match-cut to the Seeker viewfinder. Use the same image throughout the finished film.
segments.proof: Film the actual device and current app. The hero must be a real Signshot capture; the archived dinner image is a reference for the proposed scene.
segments.overlay: SIGNSHOT / A creative camera for Seeker

segments.title: Make it
segments.voiceover: Here, I’m choosing Disposable, adjusting the light, and taking the shot. The look is already in the viewfinder. It’s a point-and-shoot when you want one, with exposure, colour, and focus controls when you want more.
segments.visual: Choose Disposable, adjust brightness, tap to focus, shoot. A brief P-mode insert may show the readout; return promptly to the picture.
segments.proof: Show a visible look change in the live viewfinder, the actual shutter action, and its resulting photograph. Do not substitute a generated image.

segments.title: Keep the choice
segments.voiceover: After the shutter, I can develop the photograph, save a look for next time, or simply save and share. The original photograph stays on my phone. None of that needs a wallet.
segments.visual: Develop the photograph, briefly compare it, save the reusable look, then show ordinary Save or Share. Hold the finished photograph for a moment.
segments.proof: Capture the Develop and save-look actions as separate clean takes if needed. Show local Save/Share without a wallet prompt.
segments.overlay: Your original stays on your phone

segments.title: Choose the one
segments.voiceover: This one is worth making into an edition. I’ll call it After dinner.
segments.visual: Open Publish this moment and enter the proposed title, After dinner. Keep the photograph visible.
segments.proof: This is a proposed recording scene and title. Do not imply the archive photograph already has an edition.

segments.title: Publish five copies
segments.voiceover: Five numbered copies. I keep number one. I set the price at point zero one SOL, review the edition and costs, and approve in Seeker’s Seed Vault Wallet through Mobile Wallet Adapter. We’re using devnet and test SOL.
segments.visual: Set five total copies, price 0.01 SOL, collectors Anyone. Show the devnet badge and cost review, then the real Seed Vault Wallet approval and confirmed publication. Pause on copy 1 of 5.
segments.proof: Record the selected supply, price, audience, network, wallet approval, and confirmed result. Copy 1 is included in the total five. Pre-connect the creator wallet to keep setup out of the story.
segments.overlay: SOLANA DEVNET · TEST SOL / 5 copies · 0.01 SOL · Anyone

segments.title: What is published
segments.voiceover: Solana records the numbered Metaplex Core copies and who holds them. A public version of the photograph and its metadata go to Arweave.
segments.visual: Hold the published photograph and copy 1. A restrained two-line graphic can identify Solana and Arweave beside the actual app.
segments.proof: Use the actual published edition. The public image is a derivative; do not suggest full-size originals or image pixels are stored on Solana.
segments.overlay: Solana → numbered copies / Arweave → public image + metadata

segments.title: Signed on Seeker
segments.voiceover: A hardware key on this Seeker also signs the publication. Anyone can check that evidence. It shows which device signed it, not what was in front of the lens.
segments.visual: Open Details → Record and hold on the accepted Seeker attestation plus the app’s explanation. Keep it legible; no terminal cut.
segments.proof: The actual Record sheet must accept the attestation for this publication. Show the device verdict and its limitation together. Do not edit a failure or unavailable state into success.
segments.overlay: Device signature ≠ proof of the scene

segments.title: A copy in another wallet
segments.voiceover: Now I share the card. Its QR code opens this edition in Signshot. On a second wallet, I review the photograph, edition size, price, and additional costs. I approve the purchase. Copy two is now in this wallet; the stated price goes to the creator. It’s ownership of the collectible, not copyright to the photograph.
segments.visual: Show the real share card and QR. Cut clearly to Collector wallet; open or scan the edition in installed Signshot, review the purchase, approve, and hold on copy 2 of 5.
segments.proof: Use a distinct buyer wallet with enough devnet SOL. Show its real purchase review, wallet approval, and confirmed copy 2. Record either two devices or two clearly labelled takes on one device; do not imply two devices if there is only one.
segments.overlay: COLLECTOR WALLET / COPY 002 / 005 / SOLANA DEVNET · TEST SOL

segments.title: Why Seeker
segments.voiceover: That’s why this belongs on Seeker: photography, wallet approval, and a checkable device signature in one phone. For the mainnet release, creators can also reserve editions for Seeker Genesis Token holders.
segments.visual: Bring the photograph, wallet approval still, and accepted device record together. A small separate card describes the optional holder-only audience for the planned mainnet release.
segments.proof: The shown devnet edition must use Anyone. Mainnet Genesis Token gating is a release capability, not evidence from the devnet purchase. Do not imply SGT proves which device captured the photograph.
segments.overlay: ON SEEKER: CAMERA · WALLET · DEVICE SIGNATURE / MAINNET RELEASE: Optional Seeker-holder editions

segments.title: Back to the camera
segments.voiceover: The camera is useful every day. Editions are there for the photographs you choose. Signshot. Make the photograph. Share a copy worth keeping.
segments.visual: Return to the live camera, then finish on the hero photograph and Signshot wordmark. Allow a short clean hold.
segments.proof: End with the real photograph. No invented usage, revenue, collector count, or store availability.
segments.overlay: Make the photograph. / Share a copy worth keeping.

captureChecklist: Capture the proposed After dinner still life in the current tested Signshot release build on Seeker: viewfinder, Disposable look, brightness, focus, shutter, and resulting photo.
Capture Develop, save a reusable look, and ordinary local Save/Share as clean takes; keep private photos and notifications out of frame.
With a pre-connected creator wallet, record a real devnet publication: five total copies, 0.01 test SOL, Anyone, itemised review, wallet approval, confirmed publisher copy 1.
Record the accepted device attestation in this edition’s Record sheet, with its device-versus-scene explanation legible.
Record the actual share card/QR and a distinct collector wallet reviewing, approving, and receiving copy 2; provide enough devnet SOL for price and additional costs.
Record 3–5 seconds of clean holds on the hero photograph, publisher copy 1, buyer copy 2, and return to camera. Keep raw approval/result takes intact.
Record narration only after the demonstrated flow is verified. Narrator and footage access are unconfirmed; the script does not assume a person or voice provider.
claimLimits: This is a recording plan, not a finished video or a record of an existing After dinner edition.
The planned edition is five copies, priced at 0.01 devnet SOL, with Anyone allowed. Publisher copy 1 is included in the five; the buyer receives copy 2 only after a real successful purchase.
Keep SOLANA DEVNET · TEST SOL visible through publishing and buying. The displayed SOL price is a test amount, not revenue.
The buyer pays the stated price plus network/account/Metaplex Core costs; the stated price goes to the publisher. Do not call the purchase free or imply the total is only 0.01 SOL.
Hardware attestation proves which device signed the publication, not camera-sensor origin, scene truth, or authenticity of what was photographed.
Seeker Genesis Token ownership describes the wallet; it does not prove capture-device identity. Devnet holder gating uses stand-ins, so do not demonstrate it as real mainnet SGT enforcement.
An NFT copy conveys ownership of the numbered collectible, not copyright or exclusive rights to the image. The original stays local; publishing makes a derivative public.
The .skr name stamp is optional and can be a short deck or capture note if present on the real wallet; omit it from the main narration.
Camcorder is a still-photograph look, not video capture. Do not claim video recording.
Use actual wallet approvals and confirmed outcomes. Mark shortened confirmation waits as Wait shortened; never fabricate a success screen, photograph, or transaction result.
Only after the mainnet deployment and the exact recording build pass real phone validation, replace the devnet line with: This recording uses Solana mainnet and real SOL.
